AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Disease control? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Disease control.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Disease control.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Disease control.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Disease control.

2. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Health: Disease Control? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Health: Disease Control.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Health: Disease Control.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Disease Control.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Health: Disease Control.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agricultural Biotechnology? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Biotechnology.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agricultural Biotechnology.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agricultural Biotechnology.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Agricultural Biotechnology.

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Urban and peri-urban Agriculture? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Cropping? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Cropping.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Cropping.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Cropping.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Cropping.

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agri- business Accounts? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Agri- business Accounts.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agri- business Accounts.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agri- business Accounts.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agri- business Accounts.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Livestock Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Livestock Nutrition.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Livestock Nutrition.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Livestock Nutrition.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Livestock Nutrition.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Powered Agricultural Implements? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Powered Agricultural Implements.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Powered Agricultural Implements.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Powered Agricultural Implements.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Powered Agricultural Implements.

14. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Erosion Control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Erosion Control.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Erosion Control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Erosion Control.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Erosion Control.

16. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Forage Crops? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Forage Crops.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Forage Crops.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Forage Crops.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Forage Crops.

18. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. watt (W)

19. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Breeding? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Breeding.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Breeding.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Breeding.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Breeding.

21. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

22. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
23. In three clear sentences, explain Business and Career Opportunities in Agriculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Soil Erosion Control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Ornamental Cropping and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Protection: Disease control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Forage Crops and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Livestock Nutrition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Breeding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

30. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Health: Disease Control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
